s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of intractable hiccups with cranial nerve involvement and leptomeningeal enhancement
salient_findings: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement on brain MRI
Enhancement of several cranial nerves including bilateral vagus nerves
key_facts: Past medical history of chemotherapy and autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplant
Normal complete blood cell counts on serial monitoring
Normal neurologic examination findings except for hiccups
Brain MRI showed diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement and cranial nerve enhancement
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features
Flow cytometry showed κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation

shortlist.label: Lymphomatous meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features and flow cytometry showed κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation

shortlist.label: Neurolymphomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement and cranial nerve enhancement, consistent with neurolymphomatosis

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis and imaging studies suggest primary CNS lymphoma

shortlist.label: Secondary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's past medical history of chemotherapy and autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplant increases risk of secondary CNS lymphoma

shortlist.label: Waldenström macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features in cerebrospinal fluid and κ light chain restriction are consistent with Waldenström macroglobulinemia

raw.rationale: The presence of lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features in the cerebrospinal fluid and flow cytometry showing κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation, along with diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement on brain MRI, strongly supports the diagnosis of lymphomatous meningitis, which is characterized by the infiltration of lymphoma cells into the leptomeninges.

rejected.label: Neurolymphomatosis
rejected.why: While neurolymphomatosis involves the infiltration of lymphoma into the nervous system, the specific findings of leptomeningeal enhancement and lymphocytosis in the cerebrospinal fluid more directly support lymphomatous meningitis.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a distinct mass lesion within the brain parenchyma, which is not the primary finding in this case.

rejected.label: Secondary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's history and the specific involvement of the leptomeninges and cerebrospinal fluid are more indicative of lymphomatous meningitis than a secondary CNS lymphoma, which might involve other areas of the CNS more prominently.

rejected.label: Waldenström macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: While this condition involves a type of lymphoma, the key findings in this case, such as the specific cerebrospinal fluid abnormalities and imaging results, are more directly explained by lymphomatous meningitis.
